units.translation: Μαινάσιν [to the Maenads]. Hence they also call Semele Thyone, because Aeschylus (fr. 223) introduced her as pregnant and divinely inspired, and likewise the women who touched her belly as divinely inspired. From this it is clear, as Nauck pointed out, that the plot of the drama was the well-known story told by Apollod. 3, 4, 3 and Hyginus fab. 179, and perhaps Sophocles treated the same plot in the Hydrophoroi.
